what: R58 step 7, no step at a tile swap (fix round of Task 32, after the review's I1 and I2): the mean absolute difference of a film frame to the frame before it at each tile swap of the bend, against the mean of its two neighbours' (per 16.7 ms of film time, floored at 0.2 grey levels), home to the portfolio at 1440 by 900, three runs, with the same change with no bend (the tab's own rule `ft-glass-bend=off`) as the control. Made by make-tile-swaps.mjs and sum-tile-swaps.mjs, under the gate lock, on the production build of R58.6 (early step 0.0125, and the map's composite centred on the neutral byte 128, Ruling R130); loads at the start of the holds 2.9 (bend runs), 2.8 (control), 2.7 (strip).
target: ratio at most 1.5 (or 1.5 times the control's ratio there, floored at 1) at every swap
audit_fix: The first round's audit gave the recorder the animation's LINEAR progress (the CSS animation's timing function is the keyframes' own easing, so getComputedTiming().progress is the time fraction) and never applied the app's ease, so every tile, front and bend in the first record was wrong (labels repeated). It now applies the ease before the front and the bend, clamps the ladder as pickBendTile does and checks itself: `strictlyIncreasing` is true for every run below (the recovered tile numbers rise at every swap; `skippedTiles` lists where one frame moved two tiles). The first round's numbers, and Ruling R126 which rested on them, are withdrawn.
tiles: 64 bend tiles: tiles 0 to 35 are the early ones, fronts -0.25 to 0.1875 every 0.0125 (BEND_EARLY_STEP), tiles 36 to 63 the ladder from HAND_OVER 0.2 at steps of 8% of the radius (TILE_RATIO 1.08). A swap's tile number is the real index into BEND_TILES.
result: R58.6 (Ruling R130) did NOT remove the step. Of the 48 swaps a run (tile 9, front -0.14, to tile 60, front 1.23), all are within 1.5 of their neighbours' change (or 1.5 times the control's) in all three runs except: (1) fronts -0.001 to 0.068 (bend 0.9 to 1.0), tiles 20 to 25: ratio 2.88 to 4.08 at TWO frames a run (run 1 tiles 21 and 24 and 25 [24 and 25 are one frame], run 2 tiles 20 and 23, run 3 tiles 22 and 23), excess 0.7 to 1.5 grey levels, control 0.8 to 1.05: not tile swaps (the frames either side are identical; the step is one colour of the whole page, green at 836 ms, red and blue at 867 ms in the strip's film), the same moments as before R58.6 (one frame a run at tile 23, ratio 3.6 to 4.0, excess 1.3 to 1.55); (2) tile 58, front 1.049, ratio 1.69 in run 3 (1.54 in run 2 and 0.97 in run 1; 0.2 grey levels over its neighbours; the control 0.8 to 1.2): the late swap of Ruling R131; (3) run 1 tile 39 (front 0.261): ratio 1.73 with the control's own frame at tile 41 reading 1.88 (a screencast slip: runs 2 and 3 read 1.07 and 0.98).

half_pixel_step.finding: The one-frame step at 'tile 23' is a step of the whole page, not of the bend: outside the blob the frame before and the frame after differ by 1.3 to 2 grey levels in every colour over the whole screen (the frames either side are identical to the bit; strip rows in r58-tile-swap-strip.jpg), once, at the frame where the red push's scale passes 255 (read each frame: 232.3 at 805 ms, 255.7 at 822 ms; the filter's map has a neutral byte of 128, not 127.5, so every push is shifted by 0.00196 x its scale in pixels, and at a scale of 255 that is half a pixel: the displacement map's nearest sample takes a whole pixel). It is not made by the tile ladder: it was at the same moment with early steps of 0.025 and 0.0125, and with the peak cut from 8.55% to 7% of the height (red scale 229, under 255) the same swap reads 1.12, 1.17 and 1.26 in the three runs (counter-experiment, not committed).
half_pixel_step.since: R58.1: the lens of R54 and R56 had a red scale under 255 at every size; the hero's liquid at 150% has 280 at 1440 by 900 (2 x 1.3 x 77 px x 1.4), 262 at 390 by 844 and 349 at the 96 px cap.
half_pixel_step.not_fixed: Out of this round's scope (no new primitive; the owner picked the strength): options are a smaller red share (a peak cut to 7% of the height clears it at 900 high but changes the look), a bias cancelled by one feOffset per push (three more primitives in each filter, a per-frame cost), or accepting one half-pixel step of the page in the third of a second the bend ramps in. For the controller to rule.
half_pixel_step.r58_6: Ruling R130 built: the arithmetic composite's k2 is -128/255, so the composite is centred on the direction picture's neutral byte (unit test: a neutral direction gives exactly 1/2 at damp 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0). It does not change the displacement map's bytes: the filter stores its result in 8 bits and 1/2 is 127.5, which rounds to 128 whichever constant is used, so a neutral map is the byte 128 (0.50196) at every damp, and the displacement map's own neutral is exactly 0.5, which no byte holds. Each push is therefore still offset by 0.00196 x its scale in device pixels, whatever the constants (the old k2 -1/2 also gave 128 at a neutral texel). Measured: the step is still there at the same moments (fronts 0 to 0.07), two frames a run now. The only no-cost levers are the look (the counter-experiment of R58.4, a peak cut to 7% of the height, red scale 229 at dpr 1: 1.12 to 1.26) or the cost (one feOffset per push, three primitives a filter). At a pixel ratio of 2 the crossing is at a scale of 127.5 in CSS px, so the owner's display crosses it with every colour; not measured here.

early_step_history.0.0125 (this record): early swaps (fronts -0.14 to 0.2) 0.04 to 1.3 apart from the step at fronts 0.0 to 0.07 (see half_pixel_step): the fallback of Ruling R129.
